paper_title: Spectral Editing of Activations for Large Language Model Alignment
caption: : Left: Accuracy of all methods on each group of bias type in BBQ. Right: results on BBQ's testing set. All methods are applied on LLaMA-2-Chat-7B. For accuracy (A%_{}), higher values are better; for unknown-answer response rate (U%_{}), bias score (BS%_{}) and stereotypical response rate (SR%_{}), lower is better. We use bold font for the best result in each column, and mark the methods that improve ICL. : significant improvements on ICL in A% by pair-wise t-test with p < 0.05.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the performance of three different methods—Linear SAE, LLaMA-2-chat-7B, and ICD (Prompt version)—on the TruthfulQA benchmark as a function of the number of demonstrations used, with accuracy measured on the MCI (Mean Correctness Index) scale. The x-axis, labeled “#Demonstrations,” is linearly scaled from 0 to 2000, with tick marks at regular intervals of 500. The y-axis, labeled “MCI,” is linearly scaled from 37 to 39, with tick marks at intervals of 0.5. The “Linear SAE” method is represented by a dark blue solid line with circular markers, starting at an MCI of approximately 37.1 at 0 demonstrations and rising to approximately 39.4 at 2000 demonstrations, with intermediate values of about 38.2 at 500 demonstrations and 38.3 at 1000 demonstrations. The “LLaMA-2-chat-7B” method is shown as a magenta dashed line with circular markers, remaining constant at an MCI of approximately 37.5 across the entire range of demonstrations. The “ICD (Prompt version)” method is depicted as a cyan dashed line with circular markers, also remaining constant at an MCI of approximately 38.0 across the entire range of demonstrations. The plot indicates that Linear SAE shows a significant improvement in MCI as the number of demonstrations increases, while the other two methods show no change.
